caption: The drawing is a symmetrical architectural design featuring classical elements with a variety of colors. At the top, there is a horizontal frieze with a light blue cornice, adorned below with a red and green leaf pattern on a light background. Below the frieze, two Corinthian-style columns are depicted; each column is characterized by a blue and red twisted shaft and blue capitals with green decorative accents. The columns are set against wall panels: the left background is green with a loose floral pattern, and the right background is a gold floral motif on a pinkish base. Between the columns, a central arched niche is depicted with a blue, red, and green geometric border and a small urn or decorative finial inside, flanked by two yellow star-like motifs. Below this, in the main section, is a larger architectural structure with six twisted blue and red columns supporting an entablature and a domed roof with blue, pink, and green segments topped with a small finial. This structure forms an alcove or altar space, with a white rectangular block (possibly an altar or step) protruding from the wall. Surrounding the altar area, the wall is divided into vertical panels, alternating between a green floral pattern, a yellow floral pattern, and a pink marbled effect. To the left, a larger, fluted blue column on a white base rises along the edge. The drawing is bordered by a plain, off-white margin, and a small signature “E.F. Miller” is visible in the lower right corner.
title: Details of Wall Paintings, Side Wall of Sanctuary
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
